summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Common Cost Overruns; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [low] Atlas adds the cost of higher performance disks to regular storage costs, which may result in higher storage costs in months where Atlas provisions or replaces a node on an M40+ AWS cluster. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs.md

[low] To control costs on Atlas Infinite clusters, you set a maximum storage size when you create or modify the cluster, and Atlas blocks writes when the cluster reaches that limit. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-storage.md

[low] If you customize the amount of storage capacity, Atlas charges for the full amount of storage and does not deduct the cost of the default storage capacity. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/cluster-configuration-costs.md

[low] An underloaded server costs the customer more than necessary, while an overloaded server is bad for performance and could interfere with the scaling operation itself if it is really slammed. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/mongodb-predictive-auto-scaling-an-experiment

[low] Many teams start with larger clusters and forget to adjust as they learn their real usage patterns, leading to unnecessary costs. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md
[low] Poor schema design quietly drives up costs through inefficient queries and storage bloat. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md
